s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Female patient in her early 40s
No other medical history
No control of symptoms with topical corticosteroids
Erythematous papules and excoriations on physical examination
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Normal urine porphyrin analysis
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis
Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis
Phototest with delayed erythema to UV-A

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and germinal centers in skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate, although less typical presentation

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and scales, although less typical oral involvement

shortlist.label: Photodermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Delayed erythema to UV-A on phototest

raw.rationale: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center, along with CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, is highly suggestive of cutaneous B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not show the characteristic epidermotropism of mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy results do not match the typical findings of pityriasis lichenoides chronica, which usually shows a more superficial infiltrate.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and germinal centers is not typical of lichen planus, which usually shows a band-like infiltrate.

rejected.label: Photodermatitis
rejected.why: While the patient had a delayed erythema to UV-A on phototest, the clinical and biopsy findings are more consistent with a lymphoproliferative disorder than photodermatitis.
